cim: Can the AI boom make enough money to sustain itself?
cim_eredeti: Can the AI boom make enough money to sustain itself?
szoveg_eredeti:
Both artificial intelligence and the tricky business of valuing stocks boil down to questions of timelines. Establishing what a company is worth is a hazy exercise at the best of times, full of courageous assumptions about which cash flows will arrive when. Consider, too, timelines for AI – the years, few or many, until the technology’s capabilities surpass humans’ – and the exercise veers into incoherence.

Markets, though, do not enjoy the luxury of coherence. Take the imminent listing of Anthropic, the first big pure-play AI developer to go public. Anthropic’s prospectus touts the many remarkable (and profitable) ways in which advanced AI could transform the economy, but also warns would-be buyers off. “Our decision-making may run counter to investors’ expectations,” it says, for instance with “forward investments … that may seem irresponsibly large at first glance”.
